title: Flat base change for derived ideal-torsion local cohomology
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $IB$ denote the ideal generated by $f(I)$. For an ideal $J$ of a ring $C$, put $\Gamma_J(N)=\{x\in N:J^n x=0\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$ and $H^q_J(N)=R^q\Gamma_J(N)$ on $C$-modules. For every $A$-module $M$ and every $q\geq0$, there is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism $$H^q_I(M)\otimes_A B\cong H^q_{IB}(M\otimes_A B).$$ Tensor products and scalar extension are those of [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0ALZ (lemma-torsion-change-rings), taking cohomology for a flat map, together with Tag 0955 (lemma-local-cohomology-noetherian) to identify the closed-support construction with right-derived ideal torsion.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose a finite list $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ generating $I$, allowing $r=0$ when $I=0$. Set $u_i=f(t_i)$ and $J=IB$. Then $J=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$: every $a\in I$ has the form $\sum_i a_it_i$, so $f(a)=\sum_i f(a_i)u_i$, and each $u_i$ belongs to $f(I)$.

source.place: Tag 0ALZ (lemma-torsion-change-rings), first sentence of the proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-ideal-torsion-cech-computation] over $A$ to $M$ and over $B$ to $M\otimes_A B$. Both rings are Noetherian, and the cited result allows arbitrary modules. Write $C=C_A(t_1,\ldots,t_r;M)$ and $D=C_B(u_1,\ldots,u_r;M\otimes_A B)$ for the extended alternating complexes defined there. They are bounded in degrees $0,\ldots,r$, and the cited natural isomorphisms give $H_I^q(M)\cong H^q(C)$ and $H_J^q(M\otimes_A B)\cong H^q(D)$ for all $q\geq0$. These are the right-derived ideal-torsion groups of the statement, rather than an identification of different definitions without a comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 0956 (lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian), module assertion; this combines the closed-support computation with the Noetherian comparison of Tag 0955.

proof.text: For a nonempty increasing index set $S$, put $t_S=\prod_{i\in S}t_i$ and $u_S=f(t_S)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with both its base and algebra equal to $A$, its module equal to $M$, its second module equal to $B$, and its multiplicative set the powers of $t_S$. Its inverse gives $(M_{t_S})\otimes_A B\cong(M\otimes_A B)_{t_S}$. The latter localization is $(M\otimes_A B)_{u_S}$ as a $B$-module: by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], the fraction relation on the same numerator module is identical, since multiplication by $t_S^n$ is multiplication by $u_S^n$. Thus the coefficient isomorphism is $\theta_S((m/t_S^a)\otimes b)=(m\otimes b)/u_S^a$. This formula proves $B$-linearity (a scalar multiplies $b$), although the quoted localization theorem only explicitly asserts linearity over $A$. It is natural in $M$ by its stated naturality or directly by applying a module map to $m$.

source.place: Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), specialized to the localization coefficients in the proof of dualizing Tag 0ALZ.

proof.text: Tensoring a finite product of modules with $B$ gives the product of their tensors: the forward map is induced by coordinate projections, and the inverse inserts each coordinate by the corresponding coordinate inclusion and sums over the finite index set. The two composites are the identity by $x=\sum_S\iota_S\pi_S(x)$. Apply this in every degree of $C$, followed by the $\theta_S$ of the preceding step; in degree zero use the identity on $M\otimes_A B$. This gives degreewise $B$-linear isomorphisms $\theta^p:(C^p\otimes_A B)\to D^p$. For $S\subset S\cup\{j\}$ the face map sends $m/t_S^a$ to $t_j^a m/(t_St_j)^a$. Following either route through $\theta$ therefore gives $(t_j^a m\otimes b)/(u_Su_j)^a=(m\otimes b)/u_S^a$ in the target localization. The signs $(-1)^{a-1}$ in the alternating differentials of [lem-per-ideal-torsion-cech-computation] are unchanged. The degree-zero maps both send $m\otimes b$ to $((m\otimes b)/1)_i$. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism of complexes $C\otimes_A B\cong D$. For $r=0$ both complexes consist only of $M\otimes_A B$ in degree zero, so this construction is still the identity.

source.place: Tag 0ALZ (lemma-torsion-change-rings), equality of extended alternating localization complexes, with its finite-product and differential compatibility written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] to the bounded complex $C$ and the given flat ring map $A\to B$. Combining its canonical isomorphism with the preceding complex isomorphism and the identifications of Step 2 gives $$H_I^q(M)\otimes_A B\cong H^q(C)\otimes_A B\cong H^q(C\otimes_A B)\xrightarrow{H^q(\theta)}H^q(D)\cong H_J^q(M\otimes_A B).$$ Each arrow is $B$-linear. The flat comparison on cycle classes is $[z]\otimes b\mapsto[z\otimes b]$, so it commutes with any cochain map induced by a module map $M\to M^{\prime}$. The coefficient formula of Step 3 has the same property, and the two comparisons from [lem-per-ideal-torsion-cech-computation] are natural. Thus the composite is natural in $M$, as required. No finiteness hypothesis on $M$ or faithful flatness is used.

source.place: Tag 0ALZ (lemma-torsion-change-rings), taking cohomology in the flat case; Tag 0956 (lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian); coherent.tex Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), flatness paragraph.
